message.content:
**Progress Note – First Session**
**Client:** Roger
**Presenting Concerns:** Anxiety, Depression, Cognitive Difficulties (Focus)

**Progress:**
Roger presented to his first session reporting he is "not feeling the greatest" and is having a tough time focusing, noting that when his focus feels off, a lot of other things feel off as well. PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores of 2–3 indicate mild symptoms consistent with his reported anxiety and depression. He is currently staying at the Turning Point shelter and is collecting disability benefits for a Traumatic Brain Injury. The therapist assessed whether the cognitive symptoms related to his TBI may be contributing to both his mood difficulties and his functional impairment. A history of substance use was explored; Roger reports no current desire to use, stating it causes too many problems.

**Intervention:**
The therapist used motivational interviewing to explore Roger's values and readiness to engage in structured coping strategies, and psychoeducation was provided linking TBI-related cognitive symptoms (e.g., poor concentration) to mood dysregulation and anxiety. The therapist discussed whether Roger has access to a stable environment at Turning Point that would support consistent routine-building.

**Response:**
Roger engaged cooperatively, demonstrated insight when connecting his TBI to his mood and cognitive experiences, and collaboratively developed a behavioral activation plan for low-demand daily structure while housed at the shelter. The therapist will monitor in the next session whether Roger can identify and implement at least one cognitive strategy that improves his day-to-day focus.
